outlook.statement: NDTV is well positioned to navigate the next phase of media transformation with strong institutional capabilities, growing digital scale, and a talented team across the organisation. Focus on fortifying foundations of long-term growth – deepening technological capabilities, expanding digital reach, enhancing production infrastructure, and integrating data-driven insights.

India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 estimated at 7.6%, with Union Budget FY 2026-27 raising public capital expenditure to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, reshaping infrastructure, logistics, urban development, and digital economy.

NDTV's strategy is centred on strengthening the qualities that make journalism valuable while expanding the ways audiences encounter and engage with it, focusing on storytelling that offers context, credibility and human perspective, expanding distribution across Connected TV and OTT platforms, strengthening global reach through NDTV 24x7 International and NDTV World, building new platform partnerships (mobile apps NDTV and NDTV Profit), and launching experiential formats like NDTV Good Times.

The proposed acquisition of the "Good Times" Channel is expected to strengthen the Company's strategic positioning, diversify and expand its operational capabilities, and enhance long-term stakeholder value.

India enters FY 2025-26 with strong growth momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand, sustained public capital expenditure and improving private investment activity. As per the First Advance Estimates, real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 is placed at 7.4%. Inflation has moderated sharply, with average headline inflation declining to 1.7% during April-December 2025. The Reserve Bank of India has revised its FY 2025-26 inflation projection downwards to 2.0%, creating a supportive environment for household consumption and business confidence.

The Union Budget 2026-27 outlines a strategic shift towards sustaining growth through productivity enhancement, supply-side reforms and capacity building, while maintaining fiscal discipline. Public capital expenditure has been increased to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, reinforcing the government's continued focus on infrastructure development, logistics, urban connectivity and industrial corridors, which are expected to crowd-in private investment and support medium-term growth. The Budget places strong emphasis on manufacturing competitiveness, MSME development and critical sectors such as biopharma, clean energy, electronics.

The Indian advertising market is expected to sustain growth over the medium term, driven by continued expansion of digital channels, greater media consumption across demographic segments, and increasing participation of regional and small-medium enterprises.

The Indian M&E sector is expected to continue its growth trajectory in the medium term, with industry revenues projected to reach approximately Rs 2.86 trillion in 2026. Excluding the online gaming segment, the sector is expected to grow by approximately 8% in 2026.

Over the longer term, the sector is projected to expand at a CAGR of over 7% to reach approximately Rs 3.3 trillion (US$37.9 billion) by 2028. Digital media is expected to remain the principal growth engine for the industry.
The digital media segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 14% and reach Rs 1,640 billion by 2028.
Linear TV ad revenues are projected to decline at a net three-year CAGR of 6.8% until 2028.
Linear Pay TV distribution income likely to fall at 3% CAGR until 2028.

News TV will continue to evolve its business model with shift toward a "News+" model expanding beyond hard news into adjacent genres, premium and mass audiences addressed through distinct products and pricing, growing focus on IP led formats, branded content, events and exclusive offerings.
Connected TV will unlock product innovation with reach projected at 83 million households by 2030, creating urgency for broadcasters to monetise this audience with new products.
IPTV growth will reshape distribution and retention with bundled offerings (TV + broadband + OTT) likely to accelerate as Hybrid IPTV set top boxes merge linear TV with OTT apps.
Interactivity on TV will increase to deepen connect, with broadcasters creating more engagement-prone content to convert non-addressable Linear TV viewers into identifiable, re-targetable audiences.
Digital subscriptions are expected to continue growing at 15% CAGR over next 3 years, driven by Connected TV, smartphone penetration, and rising GDP per-capita.
SME ad spend will grow at 16% on the back of increased funding, export promotion initiatives and higher capital expenditure by the government.
The share of programmatic will continue to grow and will cross 50% of total digital media buying by 2026.

Digital Media Consumption presents an opportunity to expand digital platforms, engage with a wider audience, and deliver content through innovative digital channels, enhancing reach, brand visibility, and revenue streams.
Technological Advancements: Integration of AI, AR, and VR in content creation and delivery is creating new avenues for innovation and audience engagement.
Training and Development: Equipping workforce with requisite technical and behavioural skills through regular training helps raise quality bar and become future-ready.
Talent Attraction and retention: Recruiting and retaining the best talent to deliver value to customers and maintain market leadership.
Social Outreach Activities: Social outreach activities highly impact stakeholder relationships.
Prioritizing the expansion of its regional and global presence by demonstrating unwavering commitment to diversifying the reach and impact of its channels.

Setting goals and targets to reduce environmental impact, such as energy consumption, waste generation and water management. Exploring initiatives to increase energy efficiency, promote renewable energy sources, and implement responsible waste management practices.
Setting targets for increasing diversity in the workforce and achieving gender parity in leadership positions.
Prioritizing the health, safety, and well-being of employees through policies, trainings, and work-life balance initiatives.
